filing-20261103-5190.point: DCC says MISO's tariff names new requirements without giving their substance, and the definition and revocable exemptions add uncertainty.
filing-20261103-5190.quote: MISO’s proposed tariff revisions in this proceeding tell transmission customers that they will be subject to new reliability requirements but without providing any detail on the substance of the requirements that will be applied.

filing-20261103-5190.point: DCC says MISO keeps discretion to require compliance from customers it nominally exempts, using criteria not filed with FERC.
filing-20261103-5190.quote: MISO can unilaterally define, change, and apply reliability requirements as it deems fit and without meaningful Commission oversight.

filing-20261103-5190.point: DCC invokes the Rule of Reason: practices that significantly affect terms of service must be filed.
filing-20261103-5190.quote: where, as here, requirements significantly affect the terms and conditions of jurisdictional service, they must be included in the tariff and remain subject to Commission oversight.

filing-20261103-5190.point: DCC argues unfiled BPM requirements may be unenforceable against customers.
filing-20261103-5190.quote: raises serious questions as to whether these standards are enforceable against transmission customers at all.

filing-20261103-5190.point: DCC lists three elements a revised filing should include.
filing-20261103-5190.quote: places the substantive requirements and standards required by Section 205 and the Rule of Reason in the tariff, (2) adopts objective and transparent Large Load classification and aggregation criteria

filing-20261028-5128.point: The TDUs say MISO's answer confirms intent to exclude distribution-connected loads but does not show the Tariff language does so.
filing-20261028-5128.quote: it fails to show that this critical threshold issue is unambiguously addressed in the proposed Tariff language.

filing-20261028-5128.point: They say MISO gave no added clarity on how a Transmission Customer's agreement with a Large Load will assign compliance responsibilities.
filing-20261028-5128.quote: MISO’s Answer fails to provide additional clarity as to how it will effectuate a Transmission Customer’s agreement with a Large Load

filing-20261028-5128.point: They want the Large Load definition to say it interconnects to the transmission system, as the E-8 order's suggested definition does.
filing-20261028-5128.quote: MISO’s Tariff language should explicitly define Large Loads as those that “interconnect[] to the transmission system,”

filing-20261028-5128.point: They ask for a deficiency letter and Tariff revisions.
filing-20261028-5128.quote: The Commission should therefore issue a deficiency letter directing MISO to address these issues and require revisions to the proposed Tariff language

filing-20261013-5440.point: MISO says the pleadings broadly support the proposal and only one protest asks for rejection with refiling by end of 2027.
filing-20261013-5440.quote: only one protest requests the revisions to be rejected and MISO directed to file revised requirements by the end of 2027.

filing-20261013-5440.point: MISO says the comments offer alternatives but do not show the proposal fails section 205.
filing-20261013-5440.quote: but do not establish that the framework proposed by MISO fails to satisfy the requirements of Section 205 of the Federal Power Act.

filing-20261013-5440.point: MISO asks that the proposal be accepted without modification and without expanding the proceeding to other large-load issues.
filing-20261013-5440.quote: MISO respectfully requests that the IRR Proposal be accepted without modification and grant the requested effective date of December 4, 2026.

filing-20261013-5440.point: MISO ties the proposal to the E-8 findings on a large load definition and ongoing operational requirements.
filing-20261013-5440.quote: a definition of large load sufficient to capture loads that present the unique challenges described in the Show Cause Order

filing-20261013-5440.point: On scope, MISO says the proposal does not create a regime for distribution-connected load not taking MISO Transmission Service.
filing-20261013-5440.quote: the IRR Proposal does not create a free-standing MISO reliability regime for distribution- connected load that is not taking MISO Transmission Service.

filing-20261013-5440.point: MISO's conclusion requests acceptance without modification or condition.
filing-20261013-5440.quote: MISO respectfully requests that the Commission (i) accept this Answer and (ii) accept the IRR Proposal without modification or condition.

filing-20261002-5120.point: The Large Energy Users say the grandfathering terms balance reliability against commercial certainty for existing manufacturers.
filing-20261002-5120.quote: strike a balance between managing reliability issues caused by new Large Loads, while protecting commercial certainty for existing manufacturers and industrial customers.

filing-20261002-5120.point: They point to the E-8 order's statement that the proceeding aims at prospective reforms, not disruption of existing arrangements.
filing-20261002-5120.quote: This proceeding is not intended to disrupt existing commercial arrangements, but rather to establish prospective reforms.

filing-20261002-5120.point: They describe MISO's two exempt categories: service commencement by December 4, 2026, and MTEP 2026 or EPR-linked projects.
filing-20261002-5120.quote: Large Loads with a Service Commencement Date on or prior to December 4, 2026

filing-20261002-5120.point: They say the protestors have not shown that long-standing industrial loads cause the reliability concerns.
filing-20261002-5120.quote: The Show Cause Order is aimed at recent and exponential growth of Large Loads, not at large customers who have been reliably participating in MISO for decades.

filing-20261002-5120.point: They say cost-shift concerns belong in MISO's separate cost-shift filing, due November 16, 2026.
filing-20261002-5120.quote: these concerns are more appropriately addressed in a future filing specifically focused on cost shifting risk among transmission customers.

filing-20261002-5120.point: They argue the proposal reflects the stakeholder process and deserves deference.
filing-20261002-5120.quote: The Commission affords an appropriate amount of deference to consensus-based proposals developed during the stakeholder process.

filing-20260918-5272.point: The Midwest TDUs support swift MISO action and ask for two clarifications.
filing-20260918-5272.quote: Midwest TDUs therefore seek clarification on two issues

filing-20260918-5272.point: First, the requirements should reach only loads on the MISO Transmission System, not distribution-connected loads.
filing-20260918-5272.quote: apply to those Large Loads interconnected to the MISO Transmission System (and not to loads interconnected at to the distribution system).

filing-20260918-5272.point: Second, Transmission Customers should be able to rely on agreements with Large Loads to show compliance without undue burden.
filing-20260918-5272.quote: But additional clarity is needed to ensure that Transmission Customers can rely on these agreements to avoid undue burdens.

filing-20260918-5272.point: They ask FERC to order revisions through a deficiency letter if MISO does not clarify on its own.
filing-20260918-5272.quote: To the extent that MISO does not clarify these issues on its own, the Commission should direct it to do so in a deficiency letter.

filing-20260918-5272.point: They say the word "behind" in MISO's Large Load definition could be read to reach loads behind a distribution transformer.
filing-20260918-5272.quote: the term “behind” could potentially be read broadly to encompass anything behind such Point(s) of Withdrawal

filing-20260918-5412.point: DCC says the E-8 order settled that large loads can face distinct operational rules; the open question is whether MISO's framework is just and reasonable.
filing-20260918-5412.quote: Instead, the issue is whether the framework that MISO has proposed in this proceeding represents a just and reasonable means of mitigating these reliability risks.

filing-20260918-5412.point: DCC says the proposal leaves the covered customers and obligations unclear and moves the substance to a future BPM.
filing-20260918-5412.quote: the proposed tariff revisions do not clearly define the customers that will be subject to those requirements and the obligations that will apply.

filing-20260918-5412.point: DCC says grandfathering turns on MTEP or EPR project milestones, not on binding agreements or investments by the customer.
filing-20260918-5412.quote: MISO ties grandfathered treatment primarily to whether an associated transmission project has reached specified milestones in the MISO Transmission Expansion Plan (“MTEP”) or Expedited Project Review (“EPR”)

filing-20260918-5412.point: DCC objects to MISO's unbounded discretion to subject otherwise exempt customers to the standards.
filing-20260918-5412.quote: MISO has proposed to grant itself broad discretion to subject customers that otherwise qualify for an exemption to its reliability standards without including any objective standards or procedures in the tariff

filing-20260918-5412.point: DCC argues that leaving requirements to BPMs conflicts with FPA section 205 and the filed rate doctrine.
filing-20260918-5412.quote: Section 205 of the FPA requires public utilities to file the rates, terms, and conditions of FERC-jurisdictional service with the Commission.

filing-20260918-5412.point: DCC asks FERC to decline the filing as submitted.
filing-20260918-5412.quote: DCC respectfully requests that the Commission decline to accept MISO’s proposed tariff revisions as filed, without prejudice to a future filing

filing-20260918-5333.point: The protestors say grandfathering does not address the cost-shifting concern in the E-8 order.
filing-20260918-5333.quote: do not address the cost-shifting concerns expressed by the Commission in the Show Cause Order.

filing-20260918-5333.point: They put the exempted capacity at about 30 GW, tied to an arbitrary date.
filing-20260918-5333.quote: The proposal fully or partially exempts approximately 30 gigawatts of existing and in-flight capacity based on an arbitrary date.

filing-20260918-5333.point: They warn that grandfathered loads cause reliability upgrades whose cost lands on other customers.
filing-20260918-5333.quote: The cost of these system and network reliability upgrades will be passed onto other customers and will not be assigned to the Large Load, the cost-causer.

filing-20260918-5333.point: Local reliability costs should follow the cost-causer, and Large Loads should bear the risk if load does not materialize.
filing-20260918-5333.quote: Local reliability costs caused or materially accelerated by a Large Load should follow the cost-causer, the Large Load customer.

filing-20260918-5333.point: They want MISO's show cause proposals to apply to incremental large load coming online after December 4, 2026.
filing-20260918-5333.quote: MISO’s Show Cause proposals should apply to any incremental large new load, as defined in this filing, that comes online after December 4, 2026.

filing-20260918-5323.point: The Southern Regulators say the filing gives only a general overview that developers cannot build to.
filing-20260918-5323.quote: It lacks the specific detail needed to actually interconnect to the grid.

filing-20260918-5323.point: They warn that equipment may need costly replacement once MISO publishes the actual requirements.
filing-20260918-5323.quote: only to then replace that equipment at great expense after MISO later publishes the actual requirements.

filing-20260918-5323.point: They object to putting the requirements in BPMs, which MISO can change with little market participant input.
filing-20260918-5323.quote: when it finally develops the requirements, MISO unreasonably proposes to place them in Business Practice Manuals (BPMs).

filing-20260918-5323.point: They support Entergy's limited protest that the rule of reason puts such requirements in the Tariff.
filing-20260918-5323.quote: the Rule of Reason mandates that these requirements be placed in the Tariff where they are subject to FERC’s oversight to ensure they are just and reasonable.

filing-20260918-5397.point: The organizations say the filing lets at least 30 GW of large load ramp fast and trip offline without limits.
filing-20260918-5397.quote: give at least 30 gigawatts (“GW”) of large load, though likely more, an unrestricted ability to ramp at eye-watering speeds and trip offline unexpectedly

filing-20260918-5397.point: MISO would fully exempt loads in service by December 4, 2026 and partly exempt loads tied to MTEP 2026 or EPR projects.
filing-20260918-5397.quote: large loads with a Service Commencement Date on or prior to December 4, 2026 will be entirely exempt from any reliability requirements

filing-20260918-5397.point: They say the exemptions go beyond the Show Cause Order and shift cost from large loads to other customers.
filing-20260918-5397.quote: MISO’s proposed exemptions go far beyond what the Commission’s Show Cause Order directed, represent a broad cost shift from large loads to other MISO customers

filing-20260918-5397.point: They cite a PJM event in which 3.8 GW of load tripped, about a tenth of the load MISO would exempt.
filing-20260918-5397.quote: PJM recently narrowly averted blackouts when 3.8 GW of load–a mere tenth of the load MISO proposes to exempt–tripped offline instantaneously.

filing-20260918-5397.point: They argue MISO has not shown any study of the reliability effect of the exemptions.
filing-20260918-5397.quote: if MISO has conducted any studies or analysis of the reliability impact of its proposed exemptions.

filing-20260918-5397.point: They object that most critical restrictions sit in Business Practices Manuals, which limits enforcement.
filing-20260918-5397.quote: MISO proposes to put most of the critical restrictions of the IRR Filing in Business Practices Manuals (“BPMs”).

filing-20260918-5397.point: An attached declaration puts the exempt load near a quarter of MISO's current summer peak.
filing-20260918-5397.quote: This makes 30,000 MW more than 24% of MISO’s current peak summer demand, and 20% of MISO’s peak summer demand with the new large loads in-service.

filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.point: MISO says the filing answers some E-8 concerns (visibility, ramp rate, ride-through) and leaves study, products, cost-shift and proximate generation issues for later filings.
filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.quote: proposing visibility, ramp rate, and disturbance ride-through requirements applicable to Large Loads, along with transition provisions to minimize disruption to commercial arrangements.

filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.point: Large Load means 50 MW or more at a single substation behind one or more points of withdrawal.
filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.quote: Load with Demand of 50 MW or more associated with any facility or aggregation of facilities located at a single substation

filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.point: MISO requests a December 4, 2026 effective date.
filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.quote: MISO requests that the Tariff revisions submitted herewith be made effective December 4, 2026

filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.point: The proposal applies to transmission customers serving the load and covers four categories: visibility, PMU, ramp and ride-through.
filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.quote: The proposed framework focuses on four categories of reliability requirements that will be applicable to Large Loads.

filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.point: MISO says its study-process enhancements will come in a future section 205 filing.
filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.quote: MISO intends to address enhancements to stability assessment study processes in a future Federal Power Act section 205 filing.

filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.point: MISO lists further proposals due before the November 16, 2026 abeyance deadline, including LARS for proximate load and a Firm Service Step Up.
filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.quote: MISO is refining its Load Addition and Resource Study (“LARS”) process to facilitate the parallel study of load and generation that will address service to proximate load

filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.point: Initial ramp limits for Computational Load are 30 MW per minute up and down.
filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.quote: MISO is proposing initial up- and down-ramp limits of 30MW/minute.

filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.point: Loads with a Service Commencement Date on or before December 4, 2026 are exempt from the new Section 37A for service already procured.
filing-er26-3650-miso-irr.quote: MISO proposes to fully exempt, or “grandfather,” any Large Load that has a Service Commencement Date on or prior to December 4, 2026
